taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes the genus Anaxyrus was split from Bufo (Frost et al. 2006) and many references still use Bufo punctatus.
fieldMarks: Small toad, typically 38-64 mm snout-vent (maximum about 76 mm), females larger than males.
Dry skin, round snout and a round enlarged gland behind each eye; no bony crests between or behind the eyes.
Head, limbs and body uniform brown or grey with small warts that may or may not be tipped red.
Belly yellowish with small blackish spots; males have a dark throat.
behavior: Nocturnal; hides under moist rocks or underground by day and is active after heavy rain, including mornings and late afternoon.
Opportunistic breeder: gathers in small numbers at canyon pools and intermittent streams after spring or summer rain; males chorus in the evening.
Eats beetles, ants, bees and other small arthropods; generally inactive November-March in the north.
habitat: Rocky canyons, gullies and gypsum or limestone outcrops in deserts, dry prairies, grasslands and dry woodlands.
Eggs laid singly on plants in shallow rain pools, spring-fed pools and pools along intermittent streams.
range: California, Nevada, central Utah, Colorado and southwestern Kansas south to southern Baja California and Querétaro, Mexico, at elevations up to about 1,980 m. Not reported from Canada in the sources read.
